name: LinkedIn Newsroom
tagline: Breaking AI news to an approved LinkedIn post, from my phone

nodes.label: n8n tick
nodes.body: n8n fires every 5 minutes on India time and starts the pipeline in the background. A run lock stops overlapping runs, and a crashed run's lock expires after 90 minutes. A health check every 5 minutes restarts n8n if it jams, a queued run is stuck for 15 minutes, or the draft run goes quiet for 25 minutes, waiting 15 minutes between restarts. Each run also warns me on my phone when the LinkedIn sign in is 5 days from expiring.

nodes.label: 57 sources
nodes.body: Lab newsrooms and sitemaps, the White House and UK PM, OpenAI and Claude status pages, SDK releases, OpenRouter, Hugging Face, Techmeme, Bloomberg, CNBC, Hacker News, Reddit, Bluesky, YouTube channels from labs, the White House and CNBC, a leak tracker and Google News for the last hour. Each request gets 15 seconds and the whole sweep 50 seconds, and a broken feed only adds an error line. Sitemaps and model lists report only entries new since the last poll, and more than 25 at once counts as a site restructure, not news.

nodes.label: Fresh filter
nodes.body: Each link is cleaned of tracking tags before it is compared, so a story seen before is skipped and the earliest sighting wins. Stories older than 12 hours are dropped before any model sees them, and a date-only story passes only if it is from today or yesterday. A story counts as seen only after its rating is stored.

nodes.label: Jev rates
nodes.body: TypeSafe's Jev model answers 5 typed questions per story: impact, interest from 1 to 10, is it a launch, is it a duplicate of what I covered or posted in the last 3 days or have queued, and how much it helps my readers from 1 to 10. It rates 6 stories at a time in parallel and tries up to 4 times when the service is busy or failing.

fallback.log: Jev is offline. Claude Haiku takes over and rates the run

nodes.label: Haiku backup
nodes.body: If Jev errors, Claude Haiku rates that run in batches of 35 with the same freshness, leak and duplicate caps, but without the reader benefit score. If Jev runs out of credit, it pauses for 1 hour and tries again, so adding credit switches it back on by itself. Unrated stories carry over to the next run, and if rating fails for over 30 minutes my phone gets one alert.

nodes.label: Fixed rules
nodes.body: The rating is the higher of interest and the average of interest and reader benefit, plus 1 because Jev scores run about 1 below Haiku. Low reader benefit caps a story at 8, while leaks, stories over 6 hours old and date-only items are capped at 7, and duplicates become noise. When several stories in a run score 9 or more, one Claude Haiku check drops any that repeat the top story.

nodes.label: Dropped
nodes.body: Most stories end here. Being early only matters for the few that deserve a post.

nodes.label: Nightly digest
nodes.body: Stories rated 8 or more are held for a nightly carousel built once between 21:00 and 03:00 India time. It needs 2 to 5 stories from the last 24 hours, one per event, laid out as a cover plus one 4:5 page per story. Opus writes 120 to 200 words with a benefit line per story, and the carousel reaches my phone with the same 3 buttons. Its pages pass the same checker, layout check and render, and its text gets the same company tags.

nodes.label: PDF roundup
nodes.body: Once a day from 11:00 India time if nothing has posted in the last 24 hours, or at once when I tap Roundup now or type roundup, the run gathers unposted stories from the last 48 hours: my drafts, never ones I rejected, digests or personal posts, plus the stories the daily cap held back, with 11:00 taking only stories past their 6 hour window, so never one I could still post on its own, and a request taking fresh ones too. TypeSafe's Jev model rates each again on interest and reader benefit with none of the gate's caps, keeping the first rating, or 9, if Jev fails, and a Claude Haiku check keeps one copy of each news event and drops for good any news I posted through the newsroom in the last 72 hours in any form, my personal posts included, so the same news from several outlets appears once and news I already posted is left out, though if that check fails every story stays rather than lose one. When at least 3 score 9 or 10, the best, up to 8, become one PDF: a generated cover listing them, then each draft's original image, or for a story never drafted a page with an English headline and summary, a line illustration of the story drawn by Claude Opus and who reported it (only the feed headline and source if Opus fails), and Claude Opus writes 180 to 260 words in English only from those stories, saying no more about an undrafted one than its headline, summary or source page shows, with one fix pass if a rule check fails. The roundup reaches my phone through the company tags with Approve, Edit (type it) and Reject, where a typed change can reorder or remove its stories or swap in other unposted ones, keeping 3 to 8, and Claude Opus rewrites the text before every page and the PDF are rebuilt; every story it includes, a swapped in one too, retires so none can post alone or come back, and counts as posted once the roundup posts.

nodes.label: Daily budget
nodes.body: Only stories rated 9 or 10 are queued for their own post. At most 6 automatic drafts per India day and 1 draft attempt per run, so the feed never turns into spam, and only my Write post tap drafts past that. A queued story is drafted only while it is under 5.25 hours old. A draft that fails gets one more try on a later run.

nodes.label: Breaking alert
nodes.body: Over the 6 draft limit, each queued story still reaches my phone once as a Breaking AI news alert with its rating and 3 buttons: Read source, Write post and Roundup now. Write post sends that one story to Claude Opus at once, outside the daily cap and the 6 hour window, and the draft comes back through the checker, layout check, render and company tags to my phone with Approve, Edit (type it) and Reject, never straight to LinkedIn. Roundup now, or typing roundup on my phone, builds the PDF roundup on request from the latest strong stories. Each request waits for a running 5 minute run to finish, with a Queued notice on my phone, then holds its lock, one at a time, and my phone gets Writing your post or Building your roundup as work starts, Nothing to write when the story is gone or already covered, and Not enough for a roundup when fewer than 3 qualify.

nodes.label: Opus drafts
nodes.body: Claude Opus finds the first publication time and verifies every number and quote, keeping anything unverified out of the post. It puts reader benefit first with a For you line, then my take, the strongest counter and a question that names both sides. The post opens with how long ago the news broke, or on the news itself once it is over 8 hours old, and the card is HTML from one of the templates. If research shows the news first broke over 6 hours ago, the draft is archived before it reaches my phone, unless I asked for it with Write post.

fallback.log: Opus draft failed. My phone gets an alert and the story waits in the queue for one more try on a later run

nodes.label: Checker
nodes.body: Checks every draft for dashes, a missing age opener, length, hashtag count, bait or AI tell phrases, and a missing For you line, take or closing question. It also flags emoji in the card, a missing photo or licence credit, and motion on a photo poster. Opus gets one fix pass, and anything left reaches my phone as rule warnings.

nodes.label: Layout check
nodes.body: A headless Chrome audit checks the finished frame for text off the canvas or within 16 px of an edge, clipped or overlapping text, text under 14 px, and contrast under 4.5:1, or 3:1 for text 24 px and up. Opus fixes what it finds once, keeping 48 px margins. The frame is checked again, and anything left goes into the draft warning.

nodes.label: Card render
nodes.body: Builds the 4:5 card at 1080 × 1350 from 7 templates, never the same design twice in a row, except the plain fallback. Motion only points the eye: everything reads in frame 1, eased over 3 to 6 seconds, and loops only when natural. If motion hides content, Opus rewrites it once before the card falls back to a still. Stills and people posters with a free licence photo go out as 2x HD JPEGs, moving cards as GIFs.

nodes.label: Company tags
nodes.body: Claude Sonnet lists every company, AI lab, product, app and model named in the post and searches the web for its LinkedIn company or showcase page, reusing pages it already knows. My code then opens every page, including any Opus already chose for the draft, and keeps it only if it exists and its official name matches how I wrote it. Each page is tagged once, at its first mention, and a product gets its verified maker in front, like OpenAI's ChatGPT or Google's Gemini, unless the company is already named or is part of the product's name, like GitHub Copilot. The check runs on every draft, digest, roundup, edited version and resend on its way to my phone, where tags show in bold and a name with no page comes back as a rule warning, and it skips text it has already checked, so a plain resend costs nothing.

fallback.log: Tag check failed. The draft still reaches my phone with a tags warning

nodes.label: My approval
nodes.body: Every draft arrives as one phone notification with the card that will post (a smaller copy when the GIF is large), tags in bold, when and where the news first broke, any rule warnings, and the buttons Approve, Edit (type it) and Reject; tapping Edit makes that draft the default for my typed changes for the next hour, with an Editing this draft notice offering Type your change, Approve and Reject. When more than one draft waits, Claude Haiku sends each typed change to the draft I tapped unless my words clearly describe another, or with no tap to the one they best fit, and if Haiku fails the change goes to the draft I tapped, else the last one sent; if I say earlier changes went to the wrong draft, that draft goes back to its version from before them and the changes run on the right one. Changes typed while an edit runs wait in line as Edit queued and a double send is ignored; Claude Opus applies each change in turn, and a news draft then goes back through the checker and, when the card changed, the layout check and render, then the company tags, before it returns as the next version with the same 3 buttons; if Claude cannot be reached, my phone says so and the earlier version stays. Approve refuses a story already posted, or a single story over 6 hours old unless I asked for it with Write post, a draft with no answer for 48 hours expires, and nothing posts without my tap.

nodes.label: LinkedIn
nodes.body: Posted through the LinkedIn API as one image or GIF, a multi-image post for the digest, or a document post for either roundup PDF, with each company tagged once at its first mention. Nothing posts unless every upload succeeds, and a failed step sends the draft back to my phone, and every Approve tries again. If the post is not confirmed within 15 minutes, my phone asks whether it is already live. The Posted notice lists people to tag by hand and reminds me to reply in the first hour.

name: First to Apply
tagline: New job postings screened, priced and on my phone within minutes

nodes.label: n8n tick
nodes.body: Five steps run in order: poll, screen, price, referrals and report. Each writes its result to disk and a failed step never blocks the next, so a failure is visible instead of silent. One lock per step skips a step still running from the last tick.

nodes.label: 214 career pages
nodes.body: Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, SmartRecruiters, Workable and Recruitee publish a job the moment a company posts it, the earliest signal there is. 12 pages are read at a time with 20 seconds each, plus the Hacker News hiring thread once an hour. Only postings never seen before move on, and a page that fails shows its error in the Sources tab.

nodes.label: Title and place
nodes.body: Obvious misses stop before any model sees them: sales, recruiting, design, junior, mobile and manager titles, and places outside India, APAC or anywhere unless the job is remote with no country named. Hacker News posts get only the title check, because Jev reads their free text locations. About 88% of postings stop here.

nodes.label: Jev screens
nodes.body: Jev reads the posting against my profile and answers 7 typed questions: role family, seniority, eligible from India, fit from 1 to 10, hard blockers, stated pay against my band, and whether hidden text is trying to steer AI screeners. It takes up to 150 queued jobs a tick, 8 at a time, and tries a busy service up to 4 times, backing off between tries. Fixed code, not the model, turns the answers into keep or drop.

fallback.log: Jev failed 4 tries. These 8 jobs go back in the queue and the next tick screens them again, while this tick still releases holds and updates the sheet

nodes.label: Dropped
nodes.body: Every dropped job keeps its reason, so the screen can be audited and tuned.

nodes.label: Claude prices
nodes.body: Claude Sonnet estimates total pay at the level I would likely get, using company tiers, then writes one line on why I fit and one on the biggest risk. It prices up to 3 batches of 8 a tick and drops a job it finds closed to India or a weak fit.

fallback.log: Claude is offline. Jobs publish with Jev's verdict, pay marked not estimated yet

nodes.label: Priority rules
nodes.body: Fixed rules, so the tracker never disagrees with itself. P1: fit 70+, in band, top tier company, or an AI or forward deployed role there with pay unknown. P2: fit 70+ with a level gap, unknown or near band pay, or fit 55+ in band. Roles outside remote or my preferred cities, and services firms, stay P3 as interview practice.

nodes.label: Tracker sheet
nodes.body: Every kept job lands in the Jobs tab with its priority, fit, pay band and risk line, P1 and remote first. The Activity tab logs every step and the Sources tab shows each career page's health.

nodes.label: Referral drafts
nodes.body: For every P1 and P2 role, Claude Sonnet drafts a LinkedIn connection note and a short message with the details a referrer types into their form. The Referrals tab row also links 4 LinkedIn people searches: my network, college alumni, former colleagues and the hiring team. A P1 waits 48 hours for the referral, a P2 asks while I apply, and if drafting fails the row still lands with its searches. I send every message myself.

nodes.label: Phone push
nodes.body: Only P1 and P2 roles posted in the last 48 hours buzz my phone, and a company's first check lands quietly. One job gets its own push, a P1 with Find referrer, Draft and Job buttons, a P2 with Apply and Sheet, and several in one tick become one summary.

nodes.label: Twice daily digest
nodes.body: A second schedule refreshes my track resumes and copies them to Drive so Gmail on my phone can attach them, then sends one digest: new jobs by priority, jobs waiting for my tap, referral asks to send, follow ups due and the queue size.

nodes.label: My tap
nodes.body: I decide. The pipeline drafts everything, but finding the referrer, sending the message and applying stay with me. I update the Referrals tab, and the next tick picks up what changed. A P2 push has an Apply button, so I apply right away and send the drafted referral ask alongside.

nodes.label: 48 h hold
nodes.body: Many companies credit a referral only if it comes before the application, so a P1 waits. Every tick reads the Referrals tab and releases the job when I mark it Referred, Applied or Declined, or when 48 hours pass. A release buzzes my phone with apply now and the referral link if there is one, and a job I already applied to is released quietly.

nodes.label: Referral email
nodes.body: If I type a person with a first and last name but no email into the Referrals tab, the next tick looks the email up on free tiers and writes it back, or I type the email myself. Once the email is in, my phone gets a one tap Gmail draft with the message and the referral details filled in. I attach the resume, press Send and mark the row Asked with the date, and its follow up turns amber after 4 days if there is no reply.

nodes.label: Applied
nodes.body: The pipeline never submits an application. I get here from a P2 push, or from a P1 release whose apply now push carries the referral link when there is one, and I apply myself.

name: Inbox Triage
tagline: Every email labelled, and my phone buzzes only for the few that need me

nodes.label: Gmail
nodes.body: Apps Script on Google checks for new mail every minute, up to 15 emails a run, so it keeps working when my laptop is closed. An email that cannot be decided yet keeps its place and is tried again on the next run. It also picks up any reply my job hunt automation flags as missed, and pushes it once if it is under 3 days old. If the runs stop for 20 minutes, my Mac alerts my phone.

nodes.label: Old mail
nodes.body: The whole mailbox, about 30,900 threads, is sorted in the background sender by sender: rules and learned senders first, then Jev, then Claude. It uses at most 35 minutes a day, so live mail keeps its quota. Old mail never pushes one by one, only one summary when it is done.

nodes.label: Sheet rules
nodes.body: My own rules, mutes, clients, people, my businesses and learned bulk senders live in a Google Sheet, and the first match wins. Security codes, job alerts and known bulk senders are settled here without a model. Contact forms from my sites and mail from clients and people I know ring at once, unless their row says otherwise, and a client company's newsletters are filed without a push. Mail written straight to a business address is checked by Jev first, so cold pitches and phishing stay quiet.

nodes.label: Jev classifies
nodes.body: TypeSafe's Jev model reads each remaining email against the label descriptions in the Sheet and answers typed questions: which label, written for me or templated, asks for a reply, a real deadline, phishing. Under 60% sure, or too close between 2 labels, the email goes to Claude's queue. Phishing and text aimed at software are held for Claude without an early alert.

fallback.log: Jev is down, so the rules settle what they can and the rest goes to Claude's queue. An hourly probe switches Jev back on

nodes.label: Claude's queue
nodes.body: An unsure email is queued in the Sheet and hidden as pending, never archived. For mail from a real person a 30 minute timer starts. Answers the check rejects come back here.

nodes.label: Unsure alert
nodes.body: If my Mac is asleep, an unsure email from a real person still reaches my phone after 30 minutes as Unsure, possibly important, with the same buttons. It stays pending until Claude decides, and that later answer never pushes it twice.

nodes.label: Claude decides
nodes.body: While my Mac is awake, a background job hands Claude up to 30 queued emails at a time and keeps pulling, up to 5 batches a run, with no tools and the email text marked as untrusted data. Claude picks a label or proposes a new one, and marks an email important only when a person wrote to me personally. If a run fails, its emails return to the queue after 20 minutes and are tried again, and 2 failures in a row alert my phone. A usage limit pauses it until the reset with one push.

fallback.log: The Mac is asleep. After 30 minutes the email reaches my phone as Unsure, possibly important, and waits for Claude

nodes.label: Answer check
nodes.body: Apps Script re-checks every answer before acting on it. A new label must be at most 2 levels deep, never under Jobs and never urgent, with at most 3 a day, and it reaches my phone with an Undo button. An answer it cannot use goes back to the queue, up to 5 tries, before the email files under Other. An answer that needs a 4th new label that day waits and is tried again tomorrow. Only mail a person wrote can ring, and Claude's answers teach it bulk senders, never people.

nodes.label: Phone alert
nodes.body: Clients, customers writing to my businesses, replies from companies I applied to, recruiters writing to me, collaborations, people I know and notices with a real deadline reach my phone exactly once. Replies in one thread within 30 minutes merge into one push, and a sender I do not know rings at most 3 times a day. From 23:00 to 07:00 normal pushes are silent, while client work mail, job replies and my businesses' contact forms stay loud. If a push fails it is retried on later runs, up to 30 times, after checking it did not already arrive.

nodes.label: Gmail label
nodes.body: The label goes on once the push is settled, and Claude's answers land on the next minute's run. Nothing is ever archived, deleted, marked read or sent.

nodes.label: Silent labels
nodes.body: Most mail lands quietly in its label: bank, payments, dev notifications, newsletters, promotions and job alerts.

nodes.label: 11:00 briefing
nodes.body: One push at 11:00: counts since yesterday, threads still waiting for my reply oldest first, people whose mail was filed quietly, what Claude is still deciding, new labels and health. Senders and subjects only, never email bodies, and it is retried every 5 minutes, up to 30 times, never sent twice. On Mondays it adds how many missed alerts I tagged.

nodes.label: My tap
nodes.body: Each push has Not important, Mute sender and Mark client, and tapping it opens the thread. On a client's push Mark client becomes Open label, and Mute sender is left off for my businesses' contact forms, job replies and recruiter mail. No tap is needed: the email is already labelled.

nodes.label: Learns from me
nodes.body: Mark client adds a Clients row and moves their past mail to Clients/Work, and Mute sender adds a silent rule. Not important and my Should notify tag only suggest a change, which waits in the Sheet for my approval, as do people I email. The next email from a client then rings without waiting for Jev's verdict, and Jev only picks which client label fits.

name: Claude Watchdog
tagline: Watches every Claude Code chat on my Mac and taps me when one needs me or long work ends

nodes.label: Minute scan
nodes.body: A LaunchAgent runs one scan a minute across every Claude Code chat on this Mac: the chats themselves, their workflows, background agents, background shells and Cowork handoffs. After the Mac wakes from sleep, every timer starts fresh, so nothing looks stuck just because the lid was shut.

nodes.label: Hook notes
nodes.body: Four Claude Code hooks fire inside the chats: every finished turn, every API failure, every permission prompt or question, and every chat that closes. They leave notes for the next scan, and a turn that ran 10 minutes or more gets its Done note straight away.

nodes.label: Self check
nodes.body: A watcher that dies quietly is worse than none. If no scan has run for 10 minutes, the next finished turn sends an alert, at most once an hour, that the watchdog is not scanning, with the command that starts it again.

nodes.label: Trouble finder
nodes.body: Spots chats waiting on my Allow or answer for 2 minutes, workflows and background agents silent for 20 minutes, background shells silent for 30, chats busy for 40 minutes with no output, Cowork handoffs silent for 45 minutes, chats stopped by an API error or a usage limit, failed workflows, and questions left unanswered for 5 minutes. A chat waiting on me, a chat stuck busy, an unanswered question, a usage limit, a login or billing error and a third failure come straight to me, since a nudge cannot help. Dev servers and deliberate waits are left alone.

nodes.label: Done notes
nodes.body: Long work that finishes, a turn, a workflow, an agent or a background task over 10 minutes, gets a short Done note with the chat's own summary. It waits up to 3 minutes for that summary, so I never sit waiting on something already finished.

nodes.label: Nudge gate
nodes.body: A nudge goes out only if the owning chat is idle, not waiting on me, and its 2 nudges are not used up. A chat busy mid turn gets 10 minutes to go idle, then the item comes to me instead. A stuck shell command that touches git, ssh, scp, rsync, a push or a deploy skips the nudge and comes straight to me. A snoozed item passes as healthy until its snooze ends.

nodes.label: Haiku nudge
nodes.sub: only if the chat is idle
nodes.body: A throwaway Claude Haiku that can only send one message posts a nudge into the owning chat, at most twice per item, once for a Cowork handoff, 10 minutes apart. It also asks a chat stopped by a passing API error to continue, up to 2 retries, and asks a chat whose workflow failed to diagnose and resume it. The nudge never asks a chat to commit, push, deploy, stop or rerun anything. If a stall, retry or failure nudge is not confirmed as delivered, for example it only queues for approval in that chat, its alert goes to my phone at once.

fallback.log: Haiku could not deliver the nudge, so a Stuck alert went to my phone at once. The ladder still counts it and tries again in 10 minutes

nodes.label: Owning chat
nodes.body: The chat that started the work has the context, so it gets the first chance to fix it, or to snooze the item if the wait is expected. A chat in the middle of a turn, or waiting on me, is never messaged. Fresh output from the stuck work clears the item on the next scan. Nudges already used stay used, so a later stall on the same item comes straight to me.

nodes.label: Phone alert
nodes.body: Then my phone and my Mac get an alert: what is stuck, for how long, whether self heal was tried, and numbered steps to fix it. A nudge that could not be delivered sends its alert at once, so I can hear sooner. A chat waiting on my answer gets up to 3 alerts, 15 minutes apart.

nodes.label: My call
nodes.body: I decide what happens next. The alert has no buttons: I open the chat, snooze the item from the Mac, or let it be. The watchdog never touches the work itself.

nodes.label: VS Code
nodes.body: The alert itself queues VS Code to come forward. It comes to the front only after a minute without keyboard or mouse input, so it never steals keystrokes meant for another window. If a chat's process dies while its workflow is still running, the watchdog reopens it, at most twice, and nudges it to resume. A chat I closed on purpose only gets a notice with the steps to reopen it.

nodes.label: Snooze
nodes.body: When a wait is expected, one command on the Mac snoozes that item for a set time, or for good. Every stall nudge tells the chat how to snooze it too. Snooze covers stalled workflows, agents, shells and handoffs, not a chat waiting on me. When the snooze ends and the item is still stuck, the ladder starts again with only the nudges it has left.

nodes.label: One reminder
nodes.body: For a stalled workflow, agent, shell or handoff, one reminder follows 30 minutes later. Then it stays quiet until the item recovers; if it stalls again later it comes straight to me, with its nudges spent.

name: Self-Improving Trading Lab
tagline: A paper money research lab that improves itself and is built to make fooling itself hard
note: Paper money only. The cloud side and the daily Mac runs are live. Most ideas fail, and nothing here promises returns.
loop: Tomorrow's run is due at 7 pm

stats.label: months on paper before a change

nodes.label: Daily run
nodes.body: n8n ticks every 5 minutes and starts the day's research at 7 pm, or on the first tick after a wake, as long as it can start by 11 pm. First the lab's own copy of the code moves to the newest version; a changed dependency list stops the run until I review it. An evening the Mac sleeps through is not caught up; the next run says how many days were missed. A failed step is named on my phone and tried once more on the next tick, and a busy lab simply waits for a later tick.

nodes.label: Heads up
nodes.body: Ten minutes before a run my phone says what will be tested and whether heavy tests can run, then asks: Delay 1h, Start now or Skip today. A delay moves the run an hour and asks again ten minutes before the new time; a delay past 11 pm skips the day. No reply means the run starts on time.

nodes.label: Locked rulebook
nodes.body: The trial log, the seal, the gates, the caps and the promotion rules are locked together with every file they load, and checked against an approved fingerprint before every run and every lab command. A mismatch pauses research until I approve the change at my Mac; no phone button can loosen it. Everything else the AI may improve.

fallback.log: Rulebook changed without my approval. Research pauses until I approve at my Mac, then the next tick starts the run

nodes.label: Research atlas
nodes.body: Memory comes first. The atlas records every idea, paper, study and finding with its outcome, and a knowledge base rebuilt every run hands it all to Claude, each pattern labelled spotted, promising, confirmed or proven live. It never carries stock names, exact dates or sealed numbers, and only a proven live pattern may ever change the strategy.

nodes.label: Paper scout
nodes.body: Claude searches scholarly sites for newly published papers. Their text is treated as untrusted data: checked against a strict schema, stripped to plain text, and shown to the idea writer only inside a fenced data block. A paper whose claim can be tested is tested once on Indian data and marked replicated or refuted; the rest are filed as untested or not testable.

fallback.log: The scout failed, so today runs without new papers. It is skipped, never retried in a loop

nodes.label: Claude proposes
nodes.body: Claude reads the knowledge base and the new papers with every tool switched off, then proposes a few ideas, each with its economic reason and expected direction written down before any test. It never sees stock names, exact dates or any result after the seal, and it never grades its own ideas. At weekends it proposes no ideas, only studies and a research note.

fallback.log: Claude is unavailable or past its weekly token guard, so no ideas are proposed and the Mac spends the time on local heavy tests instead

nodes.label: Strategy menu
nodes.body: Ideas come from fixed menus across seven kinds: stock factors; market timing from the rupee, the dollar, crude oil, bond yields and fear gauges; sector rotation; calendar windows around F&O expiry and results season, with Union Budget, RBI policy and election windows waiting until their past dates are filled in with sources; risk overlays; position sizing, including a satellite of riskier bets capped at a fifth of the money; and adaptive weights, where the rule that changes factor weights is the idea under test, never weights tuned by hand.

nodes.label: Formula sweep
nodes.body: On Sundays the Mac's spare cores search thousands of formulas, on the older years only, and every formula it looks at raises the bar for every later result. On Monday the top 2 are registered as counted ideas, but only if they also hold on a held out half, which leaves Claude 2 of that day's 4 slots.

nodes.label: Trial register
nodes.body: Every idea is registered and counted before it is tested, so a failure still counts against the lab and raises the bar for every later result. At most 4 counted ideas a weekday and none at weekends, 20 a week and 500 a year. A retuned copy of an old idea, or one that behaves the same, is refused before it counts, and descriptive studies are never counted or promoted.

nodes.label: Fair test
nodes.body: Each idea is tested only on the discovery years, 2005 to 2014, from frozen history before the seal, with purged cross validation and a score discounted for every trial run so far. It must also hold as a buy-only portfolio a person could own, after costs, against the benchmark on the same days. A timing or calendar rule must beat simply staying invested, because sitting in cash is not an edge. A result that looks too good is held for audit right here.

nodes.label: Failed ideas
nodes.body: Most ideas fail. Each failure stays in the atlas with the test it missed, so it is never tried again, and it will appear on the research page with the rest of the findings.

nodes.label: Safe compute
nodes.body: Heavy tests run only on charger power, on every core but two at low priority, and the Mac stays awake for the run and no longer. Heat pressure halves the workers or pauses them, and 3 minutes off the charger stops the step; a skipped heavy step is owed to the next run. Every run measures its own time, CPU time and peak memory.

nodes.label: Cheat checks
nodes.body: A survivor must beat 200 placebo shuffles, fail on 3 random markets with no edge, keep a positive bootstrap range and survive double costs. Only then is it confirmed once on 2015 up to the seal, at most 12 a quarter. A result that looks too good is held for audit, and once a month a deliberately leaky idea must be caught, or the lab switches itself off.

nodes.label: Audit hold
nodes.body: A result that looks too good to be true stops that idea for a manual audit instead of moving on, and so does an idea that wins on a random market. In research that is almost always a bug or a leak, not a discovery. If the monthly leaky idea ever slips through, the whole lab stops itself.

nodes.label: History ladder
nodes.body: Before anything may change the live strategy it climbs a history ladder: the Indian stock history, Indian factor data from IIM Ahmedabad, US data back to 1926, and developed and emerging markets since about 1990. Each rung that applies must agree and none may contradict it. The Sensex since 1979 stays unavailable until a legal source is verified, and an idea that works only in India keeps my yearly review.

nodes.label: Exams
nodes.body: Two standing exams of the lab's judgment. Every Monday the cloud issues probability calls on the book's stocks and later scores them for accuracy and calibration against a plain base rate. On Sundays the keep or sell exam runs 5,000 realistic starting portfolios through history and grades what it keeps and sells, after costs and Indian tax.

nodes.label: Weekly round
nodes.body: On Sundays a deeper Claude round works in a throwaway copy of the code, with no commands and no web. It must advance at least one idea from my own ideas inbox, may make one small tested improvement, and can never touch the locked rulebook. Before it, a separate web-only scout files new papers, code and models as watch, trial, adopt or reject.

nodes.label: Two auditors
nodes.body: Two separate auditors read the full change and a checker scans it for stock names; then tests, typecheck and the rulebook check run in a sandbox with no network. Any failure discards the whole session. A passing change waits as a local branch for my review, never pushed and never merged by itself.

nodes.label: Findings
nodes.body: Every run writes at least one finding: a test result, a paper verdict, a study or a data note, plus a Breakthroughs section for any idea whose label moved up. No stock names and no sealed numbers, and a day with only data notes says so. Failures are kept with the rest, for the research page when it launches.

nodes.label: Cloud checks
nodes.body: The Mac hands the cloud its jobs. Survivors start paper books there, and everything after 2 October 2026 is sealed: a candidate may ask it once, after a long paper record, and gets back pass or fail with no numbers. On the first run of a month the cloud rechecks at most one pick against all 10 promotion rules, from its own records, and stages it, and the first run of a month also reruns the monthly walk-forward.

fallback.log: A cloud job failed. It is owed and runs first on the next run

nodes.label: Phone updates
nodes.body: A finish notice after every run: how long it took, CPU time, peak memory, what was tested with the reasons for each refusal, breakthroughs, heavy steps run or owed, and Claude and Jev tokens with cost estimates. A new research version is announced against the previous one, and so is every change to a strategy or to the lab itself. A failed step is named, with when it will be tried again.

nodes.label: Undo window
nodes.body: No phone tap can approve a change. A staged change reaches my phone with an Undo button: 24 hours to take it back, and with no answer it goes live at the next quarterly ranking day, at most one change a month. Later a Rollback restores the previous version exactly. Ideas that add a stock factor or a sector rotation still wait for my yearly review.

nodes.label: Paper engine
nodes.body: The live strategy trades paper money in the cloud on real prices with real costs, on a 15 minute tick, and it trades only on market days. No real money is involved. A change I did not undo applies from the next quarterly ranking day, and with no change the plan is exactly what it was. A red flag filter on company filings is wired, but the filings feeds are blocked from the cloud, so today it has nothing to read.

nodes.label: News desk
nodes.body: Every half hour the cloud may capture headlines from feeds the lab is allowed to read, match each to one company, and have TypeSafe's Jev model score it once, frozen and never rescored. No feed's terms are confirmed yet, so today it only checks which feeds answer. News cannot enter research until a clean year of archive exists.

nodes.label: Day checks
nodes.body: At 9:05, before the bell, only tested risk rules may act. At 12:30 a risk-only check reads intraday prices against the triggers fixed the evening before. Neither changes the strategy or the main book, and my phone hears only about exceptions.

nodes.label: Judgment desk
nodes.body: On each exception TypeSafe's Jev model answers one typed question: hold, exit or flag it for me. The answer acts only on the desk's own paper book, and it earns authority only if its record beats the rules going forward. Its judgment is never backtested, because the model already knows how history ended.

fallback.log: No valid answer from Jev, so the desk holds and records the refusal. The main book never depended on it

nodes.label: Closing plan
nodes.body: After the close, once the day's prices are in, tomorrow's plan fixes each holding's triggers in advance: a halt, a red flag, a fixed drop 8% below the close and a 10% price band. They never change during the day. Only a news rule that passed the same tests may change a holding; today that is the red flag veto alone.

nodes.label: Shadow books
nodes.body: Survivors run as paper books in the cloud, scored against the live strategy on the same days. Five news books compete forward beside them, including my own news-first idea and the judgment desk's book, and nothing they do touches the live strategy until their record says so.
